tasks.title: Import existing tmux panes
tasks.objective: Discover live panes from one explicit tmux server and import one unambiguous pane as a read-only Run through the tmux executable and public Control Mode.
tasks.outcome: Ctxmux clients can discover live pane associations on a selected tmux server and attach to one unambiguous imported pane while tmux remains the owner of its server, session, window, pane, PTY, and process.
acceptance: The adapter uses the tmux executable and public Control Mode rather than the private tmux socket protocol.
Import binds the complete server/session/window/pane/pane-PID identity and fails closed when a pane ID has multiple linked associations or later changes identity.
Disconnecting a ctxmux client or shutting down ctxmux does not terminate the tmux pane, session, or server.
Control Mode framing, escaped bytes, lag, teardown, and client/server version differences fail explicitly and have transcript or real-session evidence.
Behavioral differences from native Runs are documented and capability-visible without forcing an abstract Backend framework first.

verification.proves: The adapter lifecycle, ownership, transcript, public-client, and real tmux session tests pass; remote minimum/current version qualification remains separate CI evidence.

last_blocker.reason: Exact b4dcbb355a5940eea839d70dd6736a8d472b4737 is not published; required Ubuntu tmux 3.4 and macOS-current CI receipts cannot run without user-authorized GitHub publication and authenticated CI access.

tasks.title: Preserve tmux observation truth across attachment lag
tasks.objective: Make attachment fan-out distinguish replayable raw-output loss from non-replayable tmux observation loss instead of representing both with one output byte cursor.
tasks.outcome: A lagged tmux attachment either reconstructs the exact observation state promised by the Backend or fails closed with an explicit discontinuity; Gap with head_seq remains honest byte-replay evidence only.
acceptance: Gap with head_seq represents output-stream delivery loss and directs reattachment from the caller-owned cursor; replay then returns an exact retained continuation or explicit truncation without claiming every missing byte remains recoverable, and it never claims recovery for a dropped Backend observation.

If session_renamed, paused, continued, terminal, or a future non-output tmux observation can be lost, the protocol exposes an explicit non-output discontinuity or a reconnect snapshot sufficient to restore the declared observation state.

Deterministic tiny-channel fixtures mix retained output with every current tmux observation, force lag, and prove exact raw replay, no silent semantic loss, one terminal boundary, and survival of the tmux-owned pane.

Rust client, TypeScript SDK, CLI, protocol documentation, generated declarations, and runtime validation agree on the corrected boundary; any incompatible wire change advances the protocol generation without a fallback encoding.
T-002 local completion neither satisfies nor erases T-001's required Ubuntu tmux 3.4 and macOS-current receipts; T-001 is re-gated from the corrected commit before the Feature can archive.

The correction remains in generic attachment delivery plus tmux observation semantics and adds no durable event bus, public Backend trait, Agent state, tmux private-protocol support, or speculative event-sourcing framework.

verification.proves: Mixed output and tmux-observation lag, reconnect, fail-closed discontinuity, cross-client parity, generated protocol drift, and full repository regressions pass.
Replayable byte gaps and non-output observation discontinuity have distinct public semantics.
